name: Check Print Spooler Status on Domain Hosts
description: Checks if the Print Spooler service is running on target hosts. The Print Spooler is required for PrintNightmare (CVE-2021-1675) and the Printer Bug (SpoolSample) coercion attack. Running on DCs is a significant misconfiguration — DCs should never run the Spooler unless actively printing.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== WHY CHECK THE SPOOLER ===
The Windows Print Spooler (spoolsv.exe) enables two critical attacks:

1. PrintNightmare (CVE-2021-1675 / CVE-2021-34527):
   Load a malicious DLL as SYSTEM via RpcAddPrinterDriverEx
   → Direct SYSTEM code execution on the target

2. SpoolSample / Printer Bug:
   Force a machine to authenticate to an attacker-controlled host
   (MS-RPRN RpcRemoteFindFirstPrinterChangeNotification)
   → NTLM relay or NTLMv2 hash capture from the machine account
   → Used with ntlmrelayx or Responder
   → Alternative to PetitPotam for forcing DC authentication

=== WHAT TO DO IF SPOOLER IS RUNNING ON DC ===
  Option 1: PrintNightmare (direct SYSTEM on DC)
  Option 2: SpoolSample to force DC auth → relay to ADCS → PKINIT chain
  Option 3: SpoolSample → relay to another host → lateral movement

=== CHECKING VIA POWERSHELL (NO MODULE) ===
Get-Service -ComputerName ACADEMY-EA-DC01 -Name Spooler
or via registry:
Invoke-Command -ComputerName DC01 -ScriptBlock { (Get-Service Spooler).Status }

=== LINUX CHECK ===
rpcdump.py @<target_ip> | grep -i spol
or via crackmapexec:
crackmapexec smb <target> -u user -p pass -M spooler

references.title: HTB Academy - Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks

defense.why_it_works: Enumerates hosts with the MS-RPRN Print System (Spooler) exposed - the PrinterBug coercion surface for forcing authentications.
defense.prerequisites: Domain credentials and RPC reachability to candidate hosts.
defense.impact: A list of coercible hosts (Spooler enabled) for relay/coercion attacks.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1046] RPC binds to MS-RPRN across hosts; enumeration fan-out.
defense.artifacts: MS-RPRN RPC binds; the coercible-host list.
defense.prevention: Disable Print Spooler on servers/DCs that don't need it; monitor MS-RPRN enumeration; SMB signing + EPA to blunt downstream relay.
defense.evasion: A quiet, targeted RPC check per host avoids the fan-out signature.
defense.misconfiguration: Administrative shortcuts create persistent misconfigurations: passwords stored in AD Description/Info attributes (visible to all users), accounts with PasswordNotRequired flag set (blank passwords allowed), LAPS attribute readable by non-admin groups, gMSA readable by unintended principals, or SYSVOL containing scripts with embedded credentials.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Passwords in AD Description field:
Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties Description | Where-Object {$_.Description -ne $null}
# Returns: svc_backup  Description: 'Temp password: Welcome1!'

# PasswordNotRequired flag (UAC 0x20 = PASSWD_NOTREQD):
Get-ADUser -Filter {PasswordNotRequired -eq $true}

# LAPS password readable by Domain Users (misconfigured ACL):
Get-ADComputer -Filter * -Properties ms-Mcs-AdmPwd | Select-Object Name,'ms-Mcs-AdmPwd'
# Should only be readable by admins + specific LAPS readers group
defense.secure_config:
# Remove passwords from Description/Info fields:
Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties Description,Info |
    Where-Object {$_.Description -match 'pass|pwd|temp|welcome'} |
    Set-ADUser -Description $null

# Fix PasswordNotRequired accounts:
Get-ADUser -Filter {PasswordNotRequired -eq $true} |
    Set-ADAccountControl -PasswordNotRequired $false

# LAPS ACL hardening — restrict ms-Mcs-AdmPwd reads:
# Only specific LAPS-Readers security group should have Read on this attribute
# Run: Set-AdmPwdComputerSelfPermission, Set-AdmPwdReadPasswordPermission

# Audit gMSA readers:
Get-ADServiceAccount -Filter * -Properties PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword |
    Select-Object Name, PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword
